data.narrative:
Charge Robotics is a Series B–stage housing and construction robotics company founded by Banks Hunter and Max Justicz that has raised $43.9M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of four private-stage companies in the same sector (Plantd Materials, Cuby Technologies, Cover, and Somos); no directly comparable public companies exist in this niche.

The stage-progression method was applied as the primary valuation lens. Using total capital raised ($44M) as a proxy baseline and applying a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B–to-next-stage transitions, this approach yields an implied valuation of $83M. This method is applicable given Charge Robotics' current stage positioning and the maturity gradient evident in comparable private financings.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $71M to $96M, centered on a median of $83M. The relatively narrow band reflects reliance on a single triangulation method; key uncertainties include the comparability of the four private peers across capital efficiency and technology differentiation, and the degree to which market conditions since Series B close have compressed or expanded typical stage-progression multiples. Conviction in this range is moderate and contingent on closer examination of peer-level metrics (burn rate, runway, revenue traction) not available in the current dataset.
